questions.q: Why can't the DORA metrics alone tell a platform team whether developers actually enjoy using the platform?
options: DORA metrics measure delivery speed and stability, not how the work felt to the people producing it
DORA metrics are only valid for mobile applications, not platform engineering teams
DORA metrics can only be collected once a year, so they're always out of date
DORA metrics require a paid license from Google Cloud that most platform teams can't access
questions.explain: DORA metrics track delivery performance — frequency, lead time, failure rate, restore time — but say nothing about developer satisfaction, cognitive load, or whether people enjoyed the process.

questions.q: The SPACE framework for developer productivity was published by researchers including Nicole Forsgren and Margaret-Anne Storey. What problem was it specifically trying to solve?
options: The lack of any way to measure deployment frequency across large organizations
The reliance on a single activity number, such as commit count, as a stand-in for productivity
The absence of CI/CD tooling capable of running automated tests at scale
The difficulty of configuring GitOps controllers like ArgoCD and Flux
questions.explain: SPACE was proposed specifically because productivity can't be reduced to one number — especially not a raw activity count like commits or pull requests — and instead needs multiple dimensions considered together.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists dimensions from the SPACE framework as described in this lesson?
options: Scalability, Pipelines, Automation, Compliance, Encryption
Speed, Performance, Availability, Cost, Efficiency
Security, Portability, Accessibility, Compatibility, Elasticity
Satisfaction and well-being, Performance, Activity, Communication and collaboration, Efficiency and flow
questions.explain: SPACE stands for Satisfaction and well-being, Performance, Activity, Communication and collaboration, and Efficiency and flow.

questions.q: What does time-to-first-deploy measure, and why is it useful?
options: How long the CI pipeline takes to build a single pull request, independent of who authored it
How long it takes a brand-new engineer to ship their first real change to production, compressing onboarding and golden-path quality into one signal
How long a GitOps controller takes to detect configuration drift after a manual change
How long it takes to restore service after a deployment-caused production incident
questions.explain: Time-to-first-deploy tracks a new hire's path from day one to shipping a real production change, reflecting onboarding docs, local setup, golden paths, and pipeline reliability all at once.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what typically happens when a platform team measures developers purely on commit count or pull-request volume?
options: Developers automatically produce higher-quality, more reliable code as a side effect
The organization's change failure rate drops immediately because developers write smaller commits
People optimize for the measured activity itself, producing more commits and PRs without necessarily improving what the metric was meant to represent
The platform's GitOps reconciliation loop begins running more frequently to keep up
questions.explain: Measuring activity alone causes people to optimize for that activity — more commits, more PRs — which is the classic failure mode of treating a single activity metric as a target instead of one input among several.
